source: a true 3D room-decorating game (not a 2D, top-down, or UI/screen-based game): the player stands in a 3D room in third person and furnishes it by picking real furniture and props (such as a sofa, table, chair, lamp, plant, or rug) from an in-game catalog/menu and placing them into the room. Each furniture item must be a recognizable, real 3D furniture MODEL sourced from the Roblox asset library / Toolbox (search for the asset and insert the model), not a plain recolored box or a 2D image. Include a goal such as filling a set of placement slots or reaching a completion meter, and make sure placed items rest on the floor. The room and furniture must exist as 3D world objects with depth, not as a 2D/GUI layout.

answers.ask: What should the room look like - a modern apartment, a cosy cottage, a bright cartoon bedroom?
answers.answer: Make it a modern apartment room with a clean, simple interior.

answers.ask: Is completion measured by filling every placement slot, or by a percentage meter that any reasonable arrangement can fill?
answers.answer: Completion is measured by filling every set placement slot.

answers.ask: Is this one room, or a whole apartment or house of rooms to furnish?
answers.answer: This is one room to furnish, keeping the first build focused and fully playable.

## Clarifications resolved
- [author] theme — Q: What should the room look like - a modern apartment, a cosy cottage, a bright cartoon bedroom? A: Make it a modern apartment room with a clean, simple interior.
- [author] goal — Q: Is completion measured by filling every placement slot, or by a percentage meter that any reasonable arrangement can fill? A: Completion is measured by filling every set placement slot.
- [author] scale — Q: Is this one room, or a whole apartment or house of rooms to furnish? A: This is one room to furnish, keeping the first build focused and fully playable.
- [agent_inferred] slot arrangement — Q: How should the fixed furniture slots preserve a usable room? A: Distribute slots against walls and around a central conversation area, leaving a clear walking aisle from the player start to every slot.

## Enriched image prompt
Create one clean, simple modern apartment room as a true walkable 3D interior. Mark a set of floor-resting furniture placement footprints around the room while preserving a clear third-person walking aisle. Provide recognizable, full-depth 3D furniture models for a sofa, table, chair, lamp, plant, and rug, using proper asset-library models rather than plain recolored boxes or flat images. Arrange the slots so every placed item rests on the floor and a completed furnishing layout reads naturally.

## Genre
The genre is Simulation because the player repeatedly selects, places, and arranges real furniture to complete a room.

## Shape and preset
Use shared shape `interior-single`, outside Simulation's usual shortlist: the entire game is one enclosed apartment room. Preset is none because the Sandbox bundle assumes personal outdoor plots and resource collection rather than fixed interior furnishing slots.

## Config requirements
Use `buildzone-grid`, taken from Strategy, for the visible set placement footprints, rewritten as room-scale furniture slots rather than tower pads. The clean apartment shell and recognizable sofa, table, chair, lamp, plant, and rug models are scene-specific image requirements. Every model must have real 3D depth and must not be represented by a primitive box or 2D image.

## Layout requirements
Place one free-text BuildZone on every visible furniture footprint, matching its segmented size and floor position without inventing a slot count. Enforce floor contact for each placed model and leave the walking aisle outside all zones. Place one free-text SpawnZone in the clear aisle facing into the room. Catalog UI, completion tracking, and asset search are mechanics and tooling rather than placements.

## Layout components
The build contains one modern apartment room, one clear circulation aisle, a complete set of visible placement footprints, and recognizable 3D placeable models including a sofa, table, chair, lamp, plant, and rug. Keep all footprints on the floor, avoid overlap, and compose the room so both empty slot structure and a plausible completed arrangement are legible.

## Render order
Use `isometric`: the clean interior and recognizable furniture composition lead, while the simple single-room footprint can be projected afterward.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Scale is small because this is one room and individual furniture models and placement footprints must remain legible. The theme is a clean modern apartment interior. `P0` applies because the game remains inside one walkable room with no outside transition, overhang, separate map, or procedural topology.
